headline: Crude Oil Near $120 Threatens Global Economic Growth and State Budgets
summary: Crude oil traded near $120 per barrel, heightening economic headwinds and intensifying fiscal pressures, as agricultural fertiliser subsidy costs in India exceeded ₹1.03 lakh crore in five months against a ₹1.70 lakh crore target.
why: Crude oil is the world's most critical industrial commodity. Spikes toward $120 per barrel heighten imported inflation, widen current account deficits, and strain public budgets for fuel and agricultural subsidies.

impacts.name: India
impacts.why: Surging oil and feedstock prices rapidly deplete budgeted fertilizer and energy subsidies, widening fiscal deficits.

impacts.name: Energy
impacts.why: High crude prices directly expand cash flows and refining revenues for upstream and integrated oil producers.

why_moved: Elevated energy prices near $120 per barrel are generating broader inflationary risks and forcing government budget reassessments across major net-importing economies.
